note: Questions that must be answered before a decision can reasonably be made. 'Known' lists only what is verified in the repo's sources (S-ids). 'Missing' lists what is not verified. 'How to discover' lists the suggested route (see Suggestions page).

rows.question: Where can we get historical point spreads, totals and moneylines (opening and closing) for NFL games, with a licence that allows analysis?
rows.known: No historical odds dataset or line snapshot is stored in this repository. NFL.com schedule and score pages (S02) are outcome/schedule references, not the timestamped market feed required here.
rows.missing: Source, licence terms, seasons covered, and whether closing lines exist.
rows.how_to_discover: SG-03 (licensed odds vendor evaluation) or SG-04 (public-data check). Requires your choice.

rows.question: Which player-prop markets can we legally record and use, and what historical prop lines exist?
rows.known: No primary NFL policy text or approved prop-market list was retrieved for this project. The NFL Operations home is a primary-source discovery route (S04); media reports S08/S09 remain secondary and are not treated as verified policy.
rows.missing: The memo text itself, the current list of prohibited markets, and any historical prop-line data.
rows.how_to_discover: Retrieve the NFL memo primary text (F-11) and check each prop type against it.

rows.question: If real-money use is contemplated, what legal and licensing rules apply in the intended jurisdiction, including any applicable Mexican rules? Obtain qualified local advice before use.
rows.known: The reviewed Ley Federal de Juegos y Sorteos text (S05) and Cámara ficha (S06) raise permit and jurisdiction questions; this is not a legal conclusion about an individual or an online service.
rows.missing: Official SEGOB/DGJS statement on online sports betting; whether the 2023 regulation cited by secondary sources exists and what it says (F-09); whether player-side use is penalised (not stated in reviewed articles).
rows.how_to_discover: Ask the DGJS (official channel) or obtain a Mexican legal opinion. Not resolvable from sources reviewed.
rows.status: Open - legal risk, decision needed before any real-money use

rows.question: Are we building for real-money betting, paper trading (simulated bets), or research only?
rows.known: The brief asks to 'originate lines' and build 'strategies' with leaderboard rewards.
rows.missing: Your choice. Determines whether Q-03 is a blocker.
rows.source: User brief (project-scope question; not an external fact)

rows.question: What is a 'reward' for top strategies on the leaderboard: points, public ranking, or money?
rows.known: Brief says 'provides rewards for top performing strategies' with no definition.
rows.source: User brief (project-scope question; not an external fact)

rows.question: Which metric defines a 'useful' signal: closing-line value (CLV), ROI, Brier score / calibration, or a combination?
rows.known: Brief asks for 'validation gates' and 'remove luck' but does not name a metric.
rows.source: User brief (project-scope question; not an external fact)

rows.question: Can we build a multi-season injury history from the official NFL weekly reports?
rows.known: NFL.com provides an injury-report index and season/week navigation (S01). That is a discovery route, not evidence that every historical season/week is complete, consistent, or licensed for collection.
rows.missing: Whether every season/week is available in the same format; rate of access; whether the page can be scraped under nfl.com terms.
rows.how_to_discover: Sample 2 earlier weeks by hand through the fetch tool; check nfl.com terms (see Q-12).

rows.question: What are the exact official NFL injury-report rules (filing days, deadline, definitions of Out / Doubtful / Questionable)?
rows.known: The official injury-report index (S01) is the report source. The underlying policy text, filing deadlines, and definitions have not been confirmed from a primary policy document; secondary descriptions remain unverified.
rows.how_to_discover: Locate the policy PDF on operations.nfl.com (F-12).

rows.question: How many players may be active per game under the current CBA (46 or 47), and when is the inactive list due?
rows.known: The 2026 NFL Rulebook (S03) is an official rules reference but this project has not confirmed the active-player count or inactive-list deadline from it. Secondary source S13 is not accepted as verification; both figures remain unverified.
rows.missing: Primary CBA or NFL rule text for 2026.
rows.how_to_discover: Confirm in the 2026 NFL Rulebook (S03, PDF) or the CBA (F-13).

rows.question: Which official page gives each team's weekly depth chart (starter vs backup by position)?
rows.known: The injury report gives injury/practice/game-status fields, not second-, third-, or fourth-string assignments. The team directory and roster pages are discovery links and do not by themselves establish depth order; no replacement tier is confirmed.
rows.missing: Official depth-chart URL pattern and update timing.

rows.question: Are the Week 10 report entries that look inconsistent with other NFL.com content correct?
rows.known: The listed inconsistencies are preserved as report entries and review flags; no conflicting player/team/status field has been silently corrected or treated as resolved.
rows.missing: Confirmation from the player pages or the NFL.
rows.how_to_discover: Open each linked player page and compare team and status.

rows.question: Does nfl.com's terms of use permit automated collection of the injury report and schedule pages?
rows.known: NFL.com Terms and Conditions (S29) were retrieved. They state that NFL online services are for individual non-commercial/informational purposes and prohibit systematic retrieval absent express prior written consent; location-specific additional terms may also apply. No permission has been obtained for this project.
rows.missing: Whether the NFL would provide express written consent for any proposed systematic retrieval; no permission has been requested or obtained.
rows.how_to_discover: Do not automate collection. If an authorized use is needed, request express written permission and review any location-specific additional terms with qualified counsel.
rows.status: Terms reviewed; automation blocked pending express written consent

rows.question: Should GitHub Pages deployment be gated on the site-verification workflow, or should publishing and verification remain independent?
rows.known: The repository has a separate GitHub Actions verifier for both site sections and a Pages publishing workflow (S15). Verification and deployment run as separate workflows; no NFL source retrieval is configured.
rows.missing: The project preference for a required verification-success gate before deployment.
rows.how_to_discover: Review the existing GitHub Actions workflows and decide whether publication should wait for both verification jobs (SG-07).

rows.question: Should kickoff times stay in the NFL page’s published time zone or use a project-selected local time zone?
rows.known: The static injury/game rows label kickoff time as ET when copied from NFL pages (S01, S02). No local-time conversion is published and no display preference is recorded.
rows.missing: A project display preference and, if conversion is selected, a verified time-zone database/source and daylight-saving test.
rows.how_to_discover: Your choice; then verify the offset from an official Mexican time source.

rows.question: What correlation values between legs (same-game, team-total, player-prop pairs) should be used in parlay pricing?
rows.known: No NFL outcome/prop joint data or correlation value is loaded. NIST defines correlation as a relationship measure, not a joint parlay probability; official NFL data pages are only discovery sources here.
rows.how_to_discover: Compute from historical data after Q-01 and Q-02 are resolved.

rows.question: Is GitHub Pages acceptable for the live site given it is static only (no server, no live odds)?
rows.known: GitHub Pages is enabled for the repository and the current main-branch deployment was confirmed through GitHub (S15, S30). This page concerns further publication changes, not initial setup.
